newsitem.title: PERU: Peru decrees minimum wage hike for all workers.
newsitem.headline: Peru decrees minimum wage hike for all workers.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori has decreed salary rises for all workers, the Labor Ministry said Monday.
He decreed a rise in the public sector minimum wage of 16 percent.
Last week, in a State of the Nation address to Congress, Fujimori promised a minimum wage hike for public sector employees of 15 percent. Labor leaders had complained that 15 percent was not enough.
Fujimori dod not mention a private sector wage hike in his July 28 address. But hjis new decree raises the basic monthly wage in the private sector to 345 soles ($131), up 15 percent from 300 soles.
The minimum salary for public sector employees varies depending on the area of work. The government said the raise would cost the state treasury 535 million soles this year.
The last public sector minimum salary hike was a 16 percent raise last November. The private sector received a 40 percent increase in its minimum wage in April.
Annualized inflation at the end of July was 8.89 percent.
The government expects cumulative inflation this year to be nine percent, then dropping to "the level of industrialized countries" in coming years.
